To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the functor F_i applied to a module of stable constant type [1]^t gives a vector bundle whose rank is t, and the functor applied to a module with stable constant type [2] gives the dual of the original vector bundles.

for any given vector bundle E on P^r-1 there is an elementary abelian group of rank r, a field of characteristic 2 or p, and a finitely generated module of constant Jordan type such that the functor applied to the module yields the original vector bundles for p=2 or the Frobenius twists of the original bundle for p> 2, and the converse is also true.

for any vector bundle of positive rank s over projective space P^r there exists a kE-module of constant Jordan type [s] such that the vector bundle is isomorphic to the first exterior power of the bundle associated to the module, and that for odd primes p, the Chern classes of such a bundle are divisible by p.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Jordan type of a kE-module can be encoded in a vector bundle of rank r-1 over projective space.
the Jordan type of a module is a complete invariant of its isotypic component.
the Jordan type of a module can often be recovered from its vector bundle.
